special_handling: Cash is predominantly held in mainland China and is subject to remittance restrictions; discount before treating it as detachable.
Separate continuing property-management earnings from the discontinued Hong Kong lifestyle-entertainment loss.
analysis_model.reason: The audited annual report shows property management and related value-added services, not brokerage. Customer prepayments and repair funds are operating liabilities, but the business is still an ordinary fee-based operating company; therefore the ordinary owner-earnback model applies with conservative cash discounts.

assets.explanation: Bank deposits and cash; includes RMB balances and both short- and long-dated time deposits. RMB remittance restrictions and operating needs prevent treating the full balance as immediately detachable.
Repair and maintenance funds collected from property occupants/owners; economically earmarked and excluded from detachable cash.
Mainly property-management fees and other receivables. Net trade receivables were HK$52.4m; HK$7.6m was over one year old, so collection quality matters.
Property, plant and equipment, intangible assets and goodwill. These represent the operating platform and acquisition value, not readily detachable cash.

liabilities.explanation: Trade creditors, owner/occupant deposits, utility collections, related-party balances and accruals; mostly operating or on-demand obligations.
Property-management fees billed in advance; these fund future service obligations and are not financing debt.
Interest-bearing related-party amount, controlling-shareholder loans and lease liabilities; deducted in full in the detachable net-cash calculation.

owner_earnback.interpretation: After a 30% haircut to unrestricted deposits and full deduction of funding liabilities, discounted detachable net cash exceeds the supplied market capitalisation, so the formula produces a negative operating-business price and negative earnback years. This is arithmetic, not evidence that cash can be immediately upstreamed: most cash is in mainland China, the business needs working capital, and no dividend was declared. Market cap divided by discounted sustainable cash profit is about 6.0 years.

cash_breakdown.reason: 30% haircut for mainland remittance restrictions, working-capital needs and conservatism.

cash_breakdown.item: interest-bearing related-party/shareholder funding and lease liabilities
cash_breakdown.reason: Deducted in full as funding obligations.
Earmarked for owners/occupants and not detachable.

profit_adjustments.reason: Starting point; excludes the closed lifestyle-entertainment operation.
Maintenance/reinvestment proxy based on current-year purchases.
Avoid double-counting return on cash already treated as detachable; assumes 25% tax shield.
Allows for project churn, related-party exposure, receivable ageing and property-sector weakness.

dividend.forecast_basis: Board recommended no final dividend for FY2025, as for FY2024. With no established payout and mainland cash remittance constraints, the base forecast is zero rather than assuming a new distribution.

history.basis: Nil dividend disclosed in FY2025 annual report comparative.

business.one_line: AUX International earns service fees from managing residential and non-residential properties in mainland China, plus a smaller stream of community retail and household services.
business.main_business: FY2025 continuing revenue comprised HK$295.1m of property-management services and HK$35.5m of related value-added services; the Hong Kong club/restaurant operation was closed and classified as discontinued.
business.profit_source: Property management generated HK$52.5m adjusted EBITDA and is the economic core; value-added services added HK$3.0m. Continuing profit was HK$26.5m after corporate costs, depreciation, finance costs and tax.
business.business_model: A fee-based, labour- and subcontracting-intensive property manager. It collected some fees in advance, carried modest receivables and very little fixed-asset capex; profitability depends on contract mix, labour/cleaning/security costs and fee collection rather than heavy physical assets.
business.industry_position: A small regional manager headquartered in Ningbo, operating 57 projects across 14 mainland cities with 9.6m square metres contracted GFA. Project count fell from 69 while GFA rose, reflecting pruning of short-term/manpower-heavy contracts and more industrial-park exposure.

risks.evidence: HK$263.5m of bank deposits/cash was RMB-denominated and subject to mainland remittance restrictions; nevertheless no final dividend was recommended.
risks.impact: The apparent net-cash discount may persist and cash may not be readily distributable.

risks.evidence: Managed projects declined from 69 to 57 and total revenue fell 9.1%, despite GFA increasing to 9.6m sqm.
risks.impact: Further project losses or pricing pressure could reduce sustainable profit.

risks.evidence: Net trade receivables were HK$52.4m, including HK$7.6m aged over one year; gross property-management receivables carried HK$8.9m loss allowance.
risks.impact: Weak customer payment could consume working capital and lower cash conversion.

risks.evidence: FY2025 property-management revenue from controlling-shareholder-related entities was HK$50.6m and related-party balances also funded the group.
risks.impact: Economics and cash flows depend partly on transactions within the controlling shareholder ecosystem.

limitations: The requested period is 2025-12-31, but AUX International has a 31 March year-end; this annual analysis uses the latest annual report whose fiscal year ended before that cutoff, FY2025 ended 2025-03-31.

All HKD statement amounts were translated at 0.92257 CNY/HKD, the PBOC rate on 2025-04-01 as the nearest business-day proxy; income-statement flows therefore use a closing-rate approximation rather than an annual average.

The issuer does not present statutory gross profit because expenses are classified by nature. Gross profit and gross margin here are a constructed operating-contribution measure: revenue less inventory, cleaning, staff, rent, utilities, repairs and other operating expenses, before depreciation/amortisation and other income/loss.
PE TTM and market capitalisation are accepted from the supplied Tencent snapshot and were not independently recomputed.
